results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA 13.2. It notes that Supplier may assign freely without consent or notice, including to a competitor, while Customer is restricted. It explains the risk to supply continuity and to confidential specifications. It recommends a mutual consent requirement, a competitor carve-out and notice.

Issue 1 cites SA 13.3. It explains that the pending sale requires Supplier consent and can trigger termination. It recommends deleting the clause, limiting it to competitor acquirers with consent not unreasonably withheld, or obtaining a waiver before signing or closing.
The memo never mentions the automatic renewal in OF 2.2, the 30-day non-renewal notice window, or the three-year renewal terms.
Issue 2 identifies the SA 9.3 carve-out making Customer's indemnity uncapped while Supplier stays capped. It recommends capping both indemnities or making any carve-out mutual and narrow.
The memo correctly states the 12-month fees cap (9.1), Delaware governing law (12.1), and a three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
The memo states the order of precedence as SA, then OF, then Spec (SA 1.3). It applies this to the change of control issue and to the Spec's position.
Issues are explicitly ranked and tiered, with change of control first and the indemnity carve-out second, both marked HIGH.
Each issue sets out location, why it matters, and a fix with proposed language. A closing section covers open questions and business decisions.
The Specifications Schedule is expressly found to contain no issue. No statutes, cases or outside authority are cited, and the minor drafting note is not presented as a significant issue.
